content.title: About
content.content: A peanut butter and jelly sandwich consists of two slices of white bread with regular peanut butter and reduced‑sugar jelly spread evenly between them. It is a classic American snack known for its simplicity, the sweet‑salty flavor combination, and high energy content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial peanut butter and jelly sandwich recipe appeared in the United States in the early 1900s.
Peanut butter is a good source of plant protein and healthy fats.
Reducing sugar in the jelly lowers the glycemic index while preserving fruit flavor.
White bread is often chosen for its soft texture that holds the filling well.
The sandwich is a staple in school lunches and a quick snack for athletes.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Peanut butter provides about 25 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains heart‑healthy monounsaturated fats
items.content: Monounsaturated fats in peanut butter can support cardiovascular health when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Lower‑sugar jelly
items.content: Reduced sugar helps minimize rapid blood‑glucose spikes.

items.title: Source of vitamin E
items.content: Peanut butter supplies vitamin E, an antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Provides sustained energy
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates from the bread and fats with protein offers lasting satiety and quick energy.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: Peanut butter can trigger severe allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: The sandwich contains roughly 350–400 kcal, so portion control is advisable for weight‑managed diets.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some peanut butter varieties add salt; choose unsalted versions if you monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Gluten in bread
items.content: White bread contains gluten, which may be problematic for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Spread a thin layer of peanut butter on one slice of bread, then evenly spread the reduced‑sugar jelly. Place the second slice on top, optionally cut the sandwich in half. It is convenient to eat by hand and can be served with fruit or vegetable sticks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep a prepared sandwich in an airtight container at room temperature for no more than 4 hours. Store opened peanut butter and jelly in the refrigerator, and keep bread in a dry place or sealed bag to prevent drying out.
